# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 4. Parent = cand_0003 (ACCEPT, val 0.637). Scoring is a HARD restriction: the
agent's FINAL code is text-substituted `1_<id>_input`→`2_`/`3_` and RE-RUN on two hidden
input files (same layout, different data/row-counts); a task counts only if ALL 3 match
answer_position. Signatures: `[1,0,0]`/`[1,0,1]`/`[1,1,0]` = passes the preview, fails the
hidden re-run (a generalization/edge-case gap); `[0,0,0]` = wrong on the preview too
(comprehension error or environment/eval fault).

## Diagnosis summary (THIS iteration's ./trajectories/, 33 failing)
I read the FINAL emitted code + the in-trace execution outputs of the failing tasks
(delete-row group 269-44/157-4/577-40/34-5; gen-gap group 30930/32975/58890/58484/250-20/
48983/42930/49782; formula/semantic group 6698/53062/50755/585-41; transform group
398-14/413-15/55912; plus «redacted»-34/32023/146-49).
Findings, consistent with cand_0001–0003's documented harvest:
- The residue splits into (1) a RESPONSIVE **generalization/edge-case** cluster — code that
  PASSES the preview (`[1,0,0]`/`[1,0,1]`) but is subtly over-fit and drops/misplaces
  results on a hidden file with more rows or a leading/trailing partial group — and (2) an
  UNRESPONSIVE **comprehension / ambiguous-spec** cluster (`[0,0,0]`) where the code already
  generalizes but implements the WRONG operation, plus (3) **environment/eval faults**.
- The clean prose KNOWLEDGE clusters (RE-RUN/hidden-data, TYPE/FORMAT, POSITIONAL/exact
  semantics, composite-keys, BLANK-vs-ZERO, example-as-check, run/segment boundaries,
  run-to-completion) were already added by cand_0001–0003 and are load-bearing. Adding
  MORE prose restating them is the documented way to waste an iteration (the rule exists;
  the agent skips it) — e.g. 50755 SORTED despite the "second/third value = row 2/row 3,
  NOT 2nd/3rd-largest" rule; 585-41 wrote str despite the "numbers as numbers" rule.
- Comprehension `[0,0,0]` fixes are UNVERIFIABLE: no gold is in the traces or working dir
  (no input files mounted), so I cannot confirm a chosen interpretation. Editing for them
  would fail the VERIFIED + SAFE tests and risk leaking a task-specific reading → skipped.

## Ranked issue list (leverage first)
| rank | cluster | tasks (evidence) | root cause | tag | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Over-fit generalization / edge-case (passes preview, fails hidden variant) | 30930 `[1,0,0]`, 32975 `[1,0,0]`, 58890 `[1,0,0]`, 58484 `[1,0,0]`, 42930 `[1,0,0]`, 250-20 `[1,0,1]`, 48983 `[1,1,0]`, 49782 `[1,0,1]` | Code is correct on the preview arrangement but drops rows past the old extent / mishandles a leading-or-trailing partial group / a boundary the preview never exercised. The agent is TOLD to write general code (it has the rules) but does not EXERCISE the hidden-variant cases, so the over-fit slips through its own verification. | STRUCTURE (ordered, executable self-test — a new ACTION, not more prose) | **Edit A**: add a mandatory generalization self-test to the verification round of task_template.md |
| — | Comprehension / ambiguous-spec (`[0,0,0]`) | 269-44, 34-5, 157-4, 577-40, 398-14, 413-15, 146-49, 32468, 39946, 53305, 53449, 55039, 50526, 254-34, 6698, 10281 | Wrong reading of an underspecified instruction; the emitted code already generalizes. No general prose rule fixes a specific misreading, and no gold exists to VERIFY a direction. | SKIPPED (unverifiable) | not edited |
| — | Volatile "current date" | 34-5, 32023 | "current month"/TODAY() resolves differently at grade time (today=2026-08-02) vs benchmark creation | SKIPPED | not edited |
| — | Environment / eval faults | 14207 (feedback: "formula recalculation FAILED … Not a prompt defect — do not optimize against it"), 45944 (Table1 structured-ref recalc), 53062 (large-range recalc), 55912 (input xlsx unreadable by openpyxl — invalid XML), 4225 & 55258 (output provably reproduces the instruction's own stated example yet `[0,0,0]` — grader/type-coercion fault) | Infra, not a prompt defect | ENVIRONMENT (handed back) | not worked around |

## Change made this iteration (ONE edit — ADDITIVE, no global rule loosened, no deletion)
| edit | class | file | what & why it generalizes | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | STRUCTURE (worked, ordered procedure — the untried lever cand_0003 flagged) | task_template.md, verification round | New numbered step 4 "Generalization self-test": AFTER writing output_path from the real input, load a scratch copy, MUTATE it to look like a hidden variant (append rows past the last data row incl. a new group + a trailing partial group with no closing marker; change values; reorder/duplicate groups; insert a blank/text-where-number), re-run the SAME logic on the scratch copy to a throwaway path, and confirm it (i) never raises, (ii) scans to the NEW last row, (iii) gets the appended/trailing rows right. If not, derive extents/boundaries from the data and fix the GENERAL logic, then re-save output_path from the REAL input. States it is diagnostic-only and output_path is written FIRST. | BOUNDED — turns the KNOWLEDGE the agent already has (write general code; handle boundaries) into an executed CHECK, exactly the failure the over-fit cluster exhibits. It is NOT a restatement: prior iterations told the agent the rule; this makes it PERFORM the test. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- 30930 (`[1,0,0]`): writes each between-markers count only on a marker row and never emits
  the segment AFTER the last marker; passes the preview, fails a hidden file that extends
  past the last marker. Under Edit A the agent appends rows incl. a trailing marker-less
  segment to the scratch copy, re-runs, and SEES the missing trailing count → fixes the
  general logic before finishing. (Prior "boundary-cases" prose is present but was skipped;
  the self-test forces the agent to actually observe the drop.)
- 32975 (`[1,0,0]`): running max per contiguous A-run; a boundary/first-row case only
  appears on reordered/duplicated groups. Edit A's "reorder or duplicate a group" mutation
  exercises exactly that boundary, surfacing the bug on the scratch copy.
- 250-20 / 48983 (`[1,0,1]`/`[1,1,0]`): one hidden variant fails → operation is correct
  (preview passes) but an extent/boundary detail differs on more rows; the append-rows-past-
  last-data-row mutation is designed to reproduce that variant so the agent can catch it.
- Passing tasks: all 58 are `[1,1,1]` on three varying-data instances → they already
  generalize; on the mutated scratch copy their code produces correct results, the self-test
  passes, and they finish with an IDENTICAL output_path. No behavioral change.

## Confirmed-SAFE checks I ran
- Placeholders: verified programmatically — all six required placeholders + {max_turns}
  present, none unknown, after stripping the comment block. prompt.md untouched (0 edits).
- The edit is purely ADDITIVE (a new numbered step); no existing rule reworded toward a
  looser meaning, nothing deleted, no global decision/permission rule altered. It encodes
  no task id/value/date/answer — it is a general procedure over the input class.
- Regression reasoning is BEHAVIORAL: output_path is written from the real input FIRST and
  unconditionally, before the self-test; the self-test writes only to a throwaway path.
  For a correct (`[1,1,1]`) solution the self-test observes correct results and changes
  nothing saved. The only theoretical regression is the agent mis-reading its own scratch
  output on already-correct code — low, since correct general code yields correct scratch
  results.
- Did NOT re-add anything LEDGER/JOURNAL show was rejected; did NOT touch the "prefer
  literal values" line (5 passing tasks pass via formulas), did NOT re-tighten verify item
  (a) (399-14 regression under cand_0001), did NOT loosen the #N/A / lookup rules.

## Process & features used
- Direct compact dumps of all 33 failing traces (instruction + answer_position + feedback +
  final emitted code + in-trace exec outputs) via a small read-only python script, avoiding
  JSONL-transcript context overflow. Read cand_0001–0003 PROCESS + LEDGER + JOURNAL first to
  avoid re-harvesting/re-trying rejected levers. No subagents needed at this scale.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- cand_0001's RE-RUN/generalization + TYPE/FORMAT blocks, cand_0002's composite-key/
  blank-vs-zero/example/exact-semantics blocks, cand_0003's boundary + run-to-completion
  bullets — all load-bearing; keep.
- Do NOT ban Excel formulas globally (35747/37962/45581/49237/54675 pass via formulas).
- Do NOT re-tighten verify item (a) to "every cell holds a value" (399-14 regression).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why) — and the PLATEAU signal
- Comprehension / ambiguous-spec `[0,0,0]` cluster (the largest remaining, ~16 tasks):
  unverifiable without gold; every such prose edit fails VERIFIED + SAFE and risks leaking
  a task-specific reading. Not edited.
- Volatile current-date (34-5, 32023); ENVIRONMENT/eval faults (14207, 45944, 53062, 55912,
  4225, 55258) — handed back, not worked around.
- PLATEAU: the clean KNOWLEDGE clusters are exhausted; adding prose restatements of rules
  the agent already has would waste the iteration. I switched levers to STRUCTURE (an
  executed self-test) — the one untried lever cand_0003 flagged — because it is the only
  remaining way to convert the responsive over-fit cluster without more emphasis. If this
  edit does NOT clear the bar, the residual ceiling is comprehension, which prose/structure
  cannot safely close without ground truth; the honest next step is to hand back that
  ceiling with this evidence rather than ship speculative comprehension prose.
